channel.title: BUILD A CUSTOM MODULE FOR FORTISOAR :: Can't Code? No Problem
channel.description: The power of FortiSOAR is in the ability to customize solutions. The ways you can build, tweak, and polish your solutions are endless. In this section we will outline a customized module for managing the workflow to auditing existing policies on a FortiGate for our security posture hygiene. This module has been built for you to simplify the steps.

item.title: IMPORT THE SOLUTION MODULE(S) WITH PLAYBOOKS
item.description: Locate the FortiSOAR-SE_Training2023-PolicyModule.zip file that is in your downloaded all_files folder. This is a solution that we can import into your FortiSOAR instance to handle our policy management use case. Navigate to System Settings (Gear Icon at the top right). Scroll on the left pane to the bottom and click Import Wizard.

item.title: REVIEW THE POLICIES MODULE CREATED FROM THE IMPORT
item.description: Navigate to the newly imported policies Module found under Resources > Policies. Policy Records will be created in this module later in the workshop by running an automation playbook to extract policies from the FortiGate configuration. The Module configuration can be seen in System Settings>Application Editor> Modules>Policies. This is how we build what fields a record inside a module will store.

item.title: CREATE AN API ACCOUNT ON THE FORTIGATE
item.description: We want to create a new API Admin, called “fortisoar” to use the Fortigate API and extract existing policies from the configuration Access the FortiGate by clicking on the Enterprise_Core HTTPS button from your demo instance or by browsing to https://<your instance>.fortidemo.fortinet.com:14002/ Navigate to System > Administrators Create a New Rest API Admin, called “fortisoar”, in your Enterprise_Core FortiGate, using the Administrator profile of api_full and hit OK to get your API Key.

item.title: IMPORT POLICIES FROM THE FORTIGATE CONFIG
item.description: We now have a new module to store policy information and the ability to connect with the FortiGate API. The next step is to extract polices as records from the FortiGate configuration to then be audited during a SOC Policy Review. Inside Resources>Policies click on the Execute button and run the playbook called Import FortiGate Policies.

item.title: USE THE POLICY MODULE TO AUDIT AND DENY A FIREWALL POLICY
item.description: The goal of this section is to complete an audit of the firewall policy and deny a policy. The next steps on removing the policy from the network would depend on other business requirements as our objective is simply to perform an audit. Inside Resources>Polices click on secops-to-dmz to open the policy record.

item.title: USE THE POLICY MODULE TO AUDIT AND APPROVE A FIREWALL POLICY
item.description: The goal of this section is to complete an audit of the firewall policy and approve a policy. We will then update the FortiGate config with comments indicating that this policy has been reviewed. We could also put rules inside FortiSOAR to repeat this audit according to business requirements. Go back to the Policies Module and click on the dmz-to-inet record to open the policy.

item.title: USE THE POLICY MODULE TO REQUEST MORE INFO ON A FIREWALL POLICY
item.description: Sometimes we need to engage others to help us through our workflow. In this step we will reach out to another party to provide feedback for our Policy review so we can make a decision when we get a response. Inside Resources>Polices open the lan-to-dmz Policy record. At the bottom of the page, click the blue Execute button, then click “Start Policy Audit”.

item.title: CONFIRM THE CHANGES IN THE FORTIGATE
item.description: Now we can see that inside FortiSOAR we have a nice workflow indicating how many policies have been reviewed and how many are still pending. We also have some synergy in the sense that our Firewall configuration has been updated to reflect the audits performed within FortiSOAR. Note You need to hit the dropdown button to see the Audit Completion Pie Chart
